raw_line_en: ### SF-002 — Business scope and exclusions

The platform ingests enterprise documents and user-submitted cases, searches permitted knowledge, drafts grounded responses, applies deterministic risk policy, routes uncertain/sensitive recommendations to authorized reviewers, publishes through a satisfied gate, and preserves auditable evidence. Classification, retrieval, generation, policy evaluation, approval and publication are distinct activities; separate records do not require separate screens. [Source: pp.7,11–12, §§2.1–2.2; `screen_functions:r1:c4:f1`, `screen_functions:r1:c11:f1`, `screen_functions:r1:c13:f4`]
| Capability | Status and constraint | Source |
| Physical automation; irreversible financial transactions | Out of scope | p.9 §1.2.1; `screen_functions:r1:c7:f1` |
| Foundation-model fine-tuning; unrestricted browsing; agent administrative cloud permissions | Out of scope | p.9 §1.2.1; `screen_functions:r1:c7:f1` |
| Application-hosted GPU inference | Out of scope; model gateway uses external providers | p.19 §4.2.1; `screen_functions:r1:c25:f2` |
| Cross-region active/active mutation; OCR beyond English; customer-managed model weights | Deferred, not R1 features | p.10 §1.3.2; `screen_functions:r1:c8:f5` |
| Recovery deployment | One primary and one warm recovery region; primary persistent writes; snapshot restoration only under incident command | p.19 §4.2.2; `screen_functions:r1:c25:f5` |

section_en: SF-003 — Users, scopes and authorization prerequisites
SF-003 — Users, scopes and authorization prerequisites
raw_line_en: Every request binds an authenticated principal and tenant. Authorization combines role, tenant, workspace membership, case sensitivity, source ACL, action and separation of duties. Apply checks at edge, domain transaction, retrieval, tool dispatch and publication as applicable; hiding or disabling navigation is not authorization. Originating ACL filtering precedes text release to generation. Cross-tenant resource substitution returns the absent-resource not-found response class without disclosing private existence. [Source: pp.21–23 §§5.1–5.3,34 chapter9,89 TST-003; `screen_functions:r1:c29:f1`, `screen_functions:r1:c31:f4`, `screen_functions:r1:c32:f4`, `screen_functions:r1:c53:f2`, `screen_functions:r1:c141:f3`]

section_en: SF-003 — Users, scopes and authorization prerequisites
SF-003 — Users, scopes and authorization prerequisites
raw_line_en: Interactive authentication uses authorization-code flow with PKCE. Access tokens contain issuer, audience, expiry, subject and tenant; unexpected algorithms and missing tenancy claims are rejected. Do not store long-lived refresh tokens in browser local storage. Secure `HttpOnly`, `SameSite` BFF cookies are an optional source-supported alternative, not a selected architecture. Login/logout routes, session durations, refresh and expiry displays are **Needs confirmation**. [Source: p.21 §5.1; `screen_functions:r1:c30:f1`, `screen_functions:r1:c30:f5`]

section_en: SF-003 — Users, scopes and authorization prerequisites
SF-003 — Users, scopes and authorization prerequisites

[Source: p.11 §2.1.2,85 B.1,90 configuration; `screen_functions:r1:c12:f2`, `screen_functions:r1:c138:f6`, `screen_functions:r1:c142:f3`]

raw_line_en: ## Screen Inventory and Navigation
### SF-004 — Confirmed primary screens

The source names eight primary screens. Each must have **one primary action and a clear status summary**; it does not identify each primary action. Purposes below distinguish source-named screens from activity associations. Users are activity-level scope evidence, not a complete screen authorization matrix. For **every screen**, exact display conditions, browser URL, entry route, launch method and navigation origins/destinations remain **Needs confirmation**, except the citation click-through behavior in SF-008. [Source: p.57 §16.1.1; `screen_functions:r1:c96:f1`]
| Screen ID | Source name | Supported purpose/activity association | Users and open mapping | Navigation/launch evidence |

| SCR-001 | Case Queue | Case-list surface; exact queue prioritization/primary action unconfirmed | Screen matrix unconfirmed; case activities use Analyst/Reviewer scope | `GET /v1/cases?cursor=...` is a UI integration reference, not a route |

| SCR-002 | Case Detail | Navigable case workspace; individual case read/edit activities | Authorized Analyst/Reviewer reads; Owner PATCH scope mapping open | Keyboard case opening tested; exact origin and destination mechanics open |

| SCR-003 | Evidence Viewer | Source evidence inspection and citation provenance | Analyst examination/Reviewer inspection; ACL applies | Citation opens source and highlights anchored page range; mapping to this screen/window open |
| SCR-004 | Run Timeline | Human-visible run progress/trace activity | Analyst/Reviewer status and SSE reads | Run creation/progress/refresh supported; launch control and final navigation open |
| SCR-005 | Review Inbox | Recommendation review activity | Reviewer pool/role/separation rules | Review queue and decision APIs supported; queue-to-task navigation open |
| SCR-006 | Connector Health | Connector synchronization/health activity | Admin sync scope; Workspace Admin terminology open | Sync/status UI mappings and controls open |
| SCR-007 | Policy Settings | Policy administration activity | Workspace Admin responsibility; detailed predicate open | No confirmed policy-edit endpoint or setting widgets |

| SCR-008 | Audit Explorer | Immutable audit/evidence exploration activity | Auditor scope-redacted access; operator queries separately constrained | Cursor audit API; filters, row detail and export mapping open |

[Additional source: pp.57–59 §§16.1–16.2,83 A.2,89 TST-011; `screen_functions:r1:c95:f1`, `screen_functions:r1:c96:f3`, `screen_functions:r1:c96:f6`, `screen_functions:r1:c97:f1`, `screen_functions:r1:c137:f7`, `screen_functions:r1:c137:f8`, `screen_functions:r1:c137:f11`, `screen_functions:r1:c137:f12`, `screen_functions:r1:c137:f13`, `screen_functions:r1:c137:f14`, `screen_functions:r1:c137:f16`, `screen_functions:r1:c141:f11`]

`ViewState`, `ReviewForm`, `EvidencePanel` and `Notification` are logical components, not four additional screens. The same restriction applies to services, entities, events and runbooks throughout the source. [Source: pp.57,59 Figures16.1/§16.4; `screen_functions:r1:c95:f3`, `screen_functions:r1:c99:f1`]

section_en: SF-006 — Shared field-definition and interaction rules
raw_line_en: ### SF-006 — Shared field-definition and interaction rules

section_en: SF-006 — Shared field-definition and interaction rules
SF-006 — Shared field-definition and interaction rules
raw_line_en: For each field below, **all attributes not explicitly stated are Needs confirmation**: UI type, length, format, requiredness, initial value, editability, input constraints, validation timing, conditional visibility and selectable-value/data source. Domain persistence types, API types and mockup formatting are labeled separately and must not be copied into UI contracts indiscriminately. No arbitrary field defaults, numeric limits, error copy or recovery flow is authorized by an omission.

section_en: SF-006 — Shared field-definition and interaction rules
SF-006 — Shared field-definition and interaction rules
raw_line_en: Server validation occurs before transaction entry, again at domain invariants, and before tool dispatch. Endpoint-specific validation precedes allocation of long-running work. Client validation is convenience only. On unavailable dependencies, generic source contracts allow a documented retryable error **or** persisted asynchronous job identifier, never ambiguous success; selection conditions and shapes are open. GET wording does not establish universal job creation. [Source: pp.54–56 §§15.1–15.3; `screen_functions:r1:c92:f4`, `screen_functions:r1:c90:f3`, `screen_functions:r1:c90:f7`]

section_en: SF-006 — Shared field-definition and interaction rules
SF-006 — Shared field-definition and interaction rules
raw_line_en: Each actual durable-state-changing boundary record carries `tenant_id`, `revision`, `actor_id`, `occurred_at` and a correlation ID under the source's condition “wherever the operation changes durable state.” General tenant/actor boundary context remains required. These are not editable browser fields. Canonical event fields are separately `event_id`, `type`, `schema_version`, `tenant_id`, `aggregate_id`, `aggregate_revision`, `occurred_at`, `trace_id`, `payload`, using UTC/canonical JSON; aliases between the lists are not supplied. [Source: p.48 §13.1 and pp.57–59; `screen_functions:r1:c78:f1`, `screen_functions:r1:c96:f2`, `screen_functions:r1:c97:f4`, `screen_functions:r1:c98:f7`]

raw_line_en: 3. Preserve exact version provenance and authorization.

SF-008 — SCR-003 Evidence Viewer and attachment/evidence activity
raw_line_en: Destination screen/window, missing/revoked source errors, bbox rendering, page conventions and recovery remain open. Reviewers must be able to inspect source evidence **before approval**; actual recorded inspection completion is not required by supplied evidence. Access-controlled short-lived signed URLs and encryption are mandatory, but URL lifetime/expiry UX is not specified. [Source: pp.52,57–58; `screen_functions:r1:c86:f1`, `screen_functions:r1:c95:f2`, `screen_functions:r1:c96:f6`, `screen_functions:r1:c97:f2`]

section_en: SF-008 — SCR-003 Evidence Viewer and attachment/evidence activity
SF-008 — SCR-003 Evidence Viewer and attachment/evidence activity
raw_line_en: **Search:** Apply lexical and normalized vector retrieval, bounded candidates, reciprocal rank fusion, deterministic reranking, source diversity and per-query model-token budgets. Ranking is not authorization. Revoked source access must be effective **before next retrieval**, even while index cleanup is pending; source ACL changes invalidate affected cache before new results. Query fields, search placement, blank-query behavior, filtering and sorting remain open. If confidence/quality is insufficient, return `NO_SUPPORTED_EVIDENCE`, not fabricated context; clarification versus human routing needs a decision. Missing-citation generation has needs-review **or** unsupported outcome under TST-009, not a selected universal state. [Source: pp.27–29,34–36,89; `screen_functions:r1:c41:f2`, `screen_functions:r1:c43:f4`, `screen_functions:r1:c55:f1`, `screen_functions:r1:c55:f4`, `screen_functions:r1:c56:f4`, `screen_functions:r1:c141:f4`, `screen_functions:r1:c141:f9`]

SF-008 — SCR-003 Evidence Viewer and attachment/evidence activity

raw_line_en: **Run procedure:**

section_en: SF-009 — SCR-004 Run Timeline, drafting and tool activity

section_en: SF-009 — SCR-004 Run Timeline, drafting and tool activity
raw_line_en: 2. A run is created immediately; case-scoped reference acceptance returns `202`, not a completed or approved answer.

section_en: SF-009 — SCR-004 Run Timeline, drafting and tool activity
raw_line_en: 3. Subscribe to authorized SSE. Offsets increase monotonically; reconnect sends `Last-Event-ID` and backfills retained caller-scoped events.

section_en: SF-009 — SCR-004 Run Timeline, drafting and tool activity
raw_line_en: 4. Page refresh reconstructs progress from server state, not ephemeral browser memory.

section_en: SF-009 — SCR-004 Run Timeline, drafting and tool activity

SF-009 — SCR-004 Run Timeline, drafting and tool activity
raw_line_en: Expired-event history recovery, cancellation, resumability, connection errors and final navigation remain open. [Source: pp.15,40,55,58,83; `screen_functions:r1:c17:f3`, `screen_functions:r1:c66:f2`, `screen_functions:r1:c91:f1`, `screen_functions:r1:c97:f1`, `screen_functions:r1:c137:f10`, `screen_functions:r1:c137:f12`]

section_en: SF-009 — SCR-004 Run Timeline, drafting and tool activity
SF-009 — SCR-004 Run Timeline, drafting and tool activity
raw_line_en: Run catalog: `REQUESTED`, `RETRIEVING`, `GENERATING`, `POLICY_CHECK`, `AWAITING_REVIEW`, `PUBLISHED`, `FAILED`; checkpoints precede downstream dispatch. Chapter11 terminates on missing approval, budget exhaustion, repeated invalid plans, policy denial or deadline; chapter2 permits recoverable timeout. **Needs confirmation:** distinguish ordinary review waiting from absent authorization and map timeout/quota/deadline to durable status. Do not select that distinction implicitly. [Source: pp.12,41,49,82; `screen_functions:r1:c14:f2`, `screen_functions:r1:c68:f1`, `screen_functions:r1:c79:f1`, `screen_functions:r1:c137:f3`]

section_en: SF-009 — SCR-004 Run Timeline, drafting and tool activity
SF-009 — SCR-004 Run Timeline, drafting and tool activity
raw_line_en: Planner DAG depth is **8**, maximum tool invocations **16**, explicit dependencies/replayable checkpoints, with stored plan revision before side effects. Triage, Research and Draft are bounded AI responsibilities; Policy Evaluator is deterministic. Browser-supplied arbitrary tool definitions are prohibited. Discovery and model text never confer action authority. Pinned approved MCP schemas validate arguments; external writes need separate capability permission; mutable operations need idempotency and, when consequential, human authorization. A denied action cannot be replaced by a semantically equivalent tool. [Source: pp.7,40–42; `screen_functions:r1:c4:f2`, `screen_functions:r1:c4:f4`, `screen_functions:r1:c66:f1`, `screen_functions:r1:c66:f4`, `screen_functions:r1:c67:f1`, `screen_functions:r1:c67:f4`, `screen_functions:r1:c68:f4`]

section_en: SF-009 — SCR-004 Run Timeline, drafting and tool activity
SF-009 — SCR-004 Run Timeline, drafting and tool activity
raw_line_en: `knowledge.search@v1` is read-only, requires tenant-scoped `read:permitted_documents`, accepts `{query: string, case_id: uuid, max_items: int<=10}`, returns `{evidence_set_id: uuid, citations: Citation[]}`, and prohibits arbitrary URLs/filesystem access. This is a tool contract, not an editable form or page-size contract. A2A declares task/capability/input-output schema/deadline/trace and may decline; its example `case_demo` and absent output-schema field do not establish typed exceptions. [Source: pp.41,87 C.2; `screen_functions:r1:c67:f4`, `screen_functions:r1:c139:f9`, `screen_functions:r1:c139:f10`, `screen_functions:r1:c139:f11`, `screen_functions:r1:c139:f12`]

section_en: SF-009 — SCR-004 Run Timeline, drafting and tool activity
SF-009 — SCR-004 Run Timeline, drafting and tool activity
raw_line_en: Structured model parsing uses versioned JSON and bounded retries; unknown fields, invalid citations or control-character injection cause `MODEL_OUTPUT_INVALID` and no publication. Quota exhaustion is terminal for the current run, without automatic model/data-class changes. Fallback only uses approved equal-or-stronger data-handling class and approved region/deployment. Retry bounds and failure recovery remain open. [Source: pp.37–39,89; `screen_functions:r1:c60:f4`, `screen_functions:r1:c61:f4`, `screen_functions:r1:c62:f1`, `screen_functions:r1:c141:f5`]

section_en: SF-010 — SCR-005 Review Inbox and publication
SF-010 — SCR-005 Review Inbox and publication
raw_line_en: **Publication is distinct from approval.** Required evidence and satisfied versioned deterministic policy are prerequisites; unapproved high-risk runs cannot publish. Approval binds exactly reviewed content. Final-response pointer and satisfied gate commit atomically; replay cannot publish another artifact under old approval. Recompute authorization at publication after intervening tenant/document permission changes; reject stale evidence even after successful search/review. Publication invoker, endpoint/button, exact status mapping and recovery are open. Workers honor `Retry-After`, backoff/jitter, workspace quotas and fair scheduling. Deleted source tombstones schedule index removal; ACL invalidation occurs before serving new results. Incomplete provisioning is visible and blocks sync. Historic ingestion readiness uses index coverage, not queue emptiness. Schedules, quotas, coverage threshold and successful/failure navigation are open. [Source: pp.28,78; `screen_functions:r1:c43:f4`, `screen_functions:r1:c44:f1`, `screen_functions:r1:c132:f1`, `screen_functions:r1:c132:f2`]
### SF-012 — SCR-007 Policy Settings
| Setting/input family | Supported definition | Open UI attributes |
| Workspace settings | Retention class, allowed deployments, credential references, approved toolsets, reviewer routing | Widget/type/options/required/default/edit authority |
| Workspace calendar/timezone | Determines business deadlines/local display | Selection/control/source and calendar definitions |
| Policy inputs | Sensitivity, requested action, evidence quality, model class, financial impact category, confidence bands | Stored normalized with rule-set version; not necessarily editable here |
| Outcomes | `AUTO_ALLOW`, `HUMAN_REVIEW`, `REQUEST_MORE_EVIDENCE`, `DENY` | Deterministic; displayed next actions and outcome-to-lifecycle mapping open |
| Classification | Maximum included PUBLIC/INTERNAL/CONFIDENTIAL/RESTRICTED class controls route/redaction/retention/approval | Assignment/conflict/default/override policies open |

Configuration updates need revision preconditions and durable audit. Models whitelist specific approved deployments, not brands. High-impact recommendations create review tasks rather than autonomous mutations; model tags cannot override policy. No confirmed policy-save endpoint/control or quota editor exists. [Source: pp.24,37,44–45,62; `screen_functions:r1:c36:f1`, `screen_functions:r1:c60:f1`, `screen_functions:r1:c72:f1`, `screen_functions:r1:c72:f5`, `screen_functions:r1:c103:f1`]

Do not promote AppendixF policy examples (`auto_publish_classification: INTERNAL`, `require_human_review_for: [HIGH_RISK, RESTRICTED]`, `self_approval_allowed: false`) into a complete selected policy or unconditional INTERNAL publication permission. [Source: p.90; `screen_functions:r1:c142:f3`]

# 2. API Specification
## API Inventory and Responsibilities
### API-001 — Scope, authority and traceability

**Confirmed.** This specification describes the APIs of OrionDesk AI, `OD-AI-DDS-001`, `R1.0`, design revision `1.3`, a controlled fictional reference architecture. All citations below refer to **1794353355-OrionDesk_AI_Detailed_Design_Specification.pdf**, using original pages and supplied finding IDs. The root has reconciled the supplied chapter outcomes; it does not claim a new inspection of unavailable attachments. The candidate remains provisional pending evidence review.

The source states: **“All numbers are design assumptions, not measured production performance.”** Figures illustrate normative boundaries, not generated implementation artifacts. Fictional identities, UI values, grants, times and configuration examples are not production defaults or evidence of approval. **Confirmed** identifies reference-system requirements; **Needs confirmation** identifies incomplete contracts or unresolved choices; **Proposal** would identify a suggested design. No new design proposal is selected here. `API-*` identifiers in this file are specification-assigned, not source namespace mappings. [Source: pp.1–2,8; `api:r1:c1:f1`, `api:r1:c1:f2`, `api:r1:c2:f1`, `api:r1:c2:f2`, `api:r1:c5:f1`]

The API scope includes enterprise document ingestion, permission-aware retrieval, grounded drafting, deterministic policy, human review, publication, audit and controlled operations. Physical automation, irreversible financial transactions, foundation-model fine-tuning, unrestricted browsing and agent cloud-administration permissions are **Out of scope**. Application-hosted GPU inference is excluded. Cross-region active/active mutation, OCR beyond English and customer-managed model weights are deferred. [Source: pp.7,9–10,19; `api:r1:c4:f1`, `api:r1:c7:f1`, `api:r1:c8:f5`, `api:r1:c25:f2`]

References to [01_screen_functions.md](01_screen_functions.md) preserve `SCR-001`–`SCR-008` and `SF-*`. They are activity associations, not browser routes or a complete caller permission matrix. No endpoint establishes an additional screen. Screen/figure aliases remain unresolved under `SF-005` and `SF-020 OQ-001`.
### API-002 — Shared authentication and authorization

Every request binds an authenticated principal and tenant. Authorization combines role, tenant, workspace membership, resource attributes, case sensitivity, originating document ACL, action and separation of duties. Apply it at edge, domain transaction, retrieval, tool dispatch and publication as applicable. Navigation hiding is not authorization. Baseline roles are `Analyst`, `Reviewer`, `Admin`, `Auditor`, `Service`; Appendix A's `Owner`, `Member` and `approver` scopes require mapping. `Workspace Admin` is not silently equated with `Admin`. [Source: pp.11,21–23,41,83; `api:r1:c12:f1`, `api:r1:c29:f1`, `api:r1:c31:f1`, `api:r1:c31:f5`, `api:r1:c67:f1`, `api:r1:c137:f8`, `api:r1:c137:f15`]

| Browser storage | No long-lived refresh tokens in local storage | Session implementation |
| Optional BFF | Secure `HttpOnly`, `SameSite` cookies may be issued | Selection, cookie name/value, CSRF and session contracts |

| Internal HTTP/RPC | Scoped identities; mTLS-authenticated HTTP or gRPC; generated/versioned contracts and independent authorization; audience/scoped IAM checks; do not share identities between deployment units | Protocol per interface, claims/grants and audience values |
| Provider calls | Controlled egress; only scoped model context/structured prompts, never raw connector tokens or unrestricted database access | Selected providers/endpoints/regions |
| MCP/A2A | Separate invoking-principal/workspace-policy/tool-scope/data-classification authorization; discovery never grants capability permission | Grant resolution and transport |

The orchestrator has **no direct database credentials** and uses narrowly scoped APIs. Datastores are private; public TLS terminates at the gateway forwarding to private API workloads. [Source: pp.9,18; `api:r1:c8:f1`, `api:r1:c24:f1`]

`knowledge.search@v1` requires `read:permitted_documents`, tenant-scoped. It is read-only with **no arbitrary URLs or filesystem access**. Approved MCP schemas are version-pinned and arguments validated. Tool transport/method/path/status/error envelope remains **Needs confirmation**. A2A carries task ID, capability reference, declared input/output schema, deadline and trace context. Receiver may decline. Registration/discovery does not authorize invocation. The source's **illustrative example**, not a proposed or complete normative schema, is:

{"task_id":"019ac000-0000-7000-8000-000000000042","tenant_id":"tenant_example_01","capability":"research.grounded_search.v1","input_schema":"schema://oriondesk/research-request/1","deadline_at":"2026-11-09T08:00:00Z","trace_id":"trace_example_01","authorization_ref":"grant_readonly_14","payload":{"case_id":"case_demo","query":"..."}}

**Needs confirmation:** requiredness/types/schema contents/output schema, grant lifetime/verification, transport, decline and deadline handling, and `case_demo` handoff to typed MCP UUID. The omission of `output_schema` and placeholder case does not establish an exception. [Source: pp.41,87; `api:r1:c67:f5`, `api:r1:c139:f9`, `api:r1:c139:f13`, `api:r1:c139:f14`]

raw_line_en: ### API-050 — Connector synchronization and retrieval
**Synchronization:**
1. Block sync if provisioning incomplete; show incomplete state.
2. Advertise list/fetch/delta cursor/ACL/delete. Unsupported capability yields lower-trust mode and explicit visible warning, never ACL bypass.
3. Store workspace vault credential references. Revoked queued jobs fail `CONNECTOR_REAUTH_REQUIRED` without tokens; running-job behavior remains open.
4. Persist provider cursor/high-watermark/error ledger. Advance only after durable preceding outcomes; retry partial batches safely.

5. Honor `Retry-After`, exponential backoff/jitter, workspace quotas and fair scheduling. After bounded retries, malformed item quarantine includes reason/correlation/remediation; recorded ledger exception **permits** remaining batch continuation.
6. Source deletion tombstones/schedules index removal. Source ACL changes invalidate affected caches before new results; revoked access applies **before next retrieval**, not after cleanup.
7. Backfill bounded windows/stable source IDs/per-batch receipts; readiness uses index coverage, not queue emptiness.

**Retrieval:** ACL filtering precedes generation text release; relevance never grants access. Form lexical/normalized vector queries, bound candidates, RRF merge, deterministic rerank, diversify documents/sources and cap model-context tokens. Internal search rows retain tenant/workspace/version/chunk/language/classification, normalized text and **1536-dimensional embeddings**. Parallel rebuilds atomically switch read alias only after completeness/recall checks; database remains authoritative. Cache keys include tenant, user-scope digest, source ACL revision, query hash and index generation. Permission change purges affected cache before TTL and next-query access remains mandatory. Insufficient quality/confidence returns `NO_SUPPORTED_EVIDENCE`, never fabricated context; clarification versus human route is unresolved. [Source: pp.34–36,53; `api:r1:c53:f2`, `api:r1:c54:f1`, `api:r1:c54:f5`, `api:r1:c55:f1`, `api:r1:c55:f4`, `api:r1:c56:f5`, `api:r1:c86:f7`]

Source opening is authorized, encrypted and via access-controlled short-lived signed URLs with opaque public names. URL expiry/revocation/page/bbox contracts remain open. Authorized evidence interfaces do not permit documents in errors/diagnostic telemetry. [Source: pp.52,57,84; `api:r1:c86:f1`, `api:r1:c86:f2`, `api:r1:c96:f6`, `api:r1:c137:f22`]

API-054 — Controlled exit, operations and recovery
raw_line_en: Export/delete both require **two independent approval checks**; export explicitly requires **two-person approval plus manifest**, and a single Admin fails. Export includes case metadata, approved artifacts, source references and checksum audit manifests; exclude secrets/internal prompts. Deletion applies holds/tombstones/blob/index removal/completion receipts. Held protected records are retained and receipted. Data-subject requests use the same inventory, not a newly invented endpoint. Manifest/receipt/checksum/approval/download/status and partial-failure schemas remain open. raw_line_en: Audit is append-only/batch-hash chained and independently retained; operators may query, not alter historical decisions. raw_line_en: ### API-057 — Concrete verification obligations
Tests below are required, **not reported passed**. They preserve preceding `SF-019 AC-*` associations without inventing namespace equivalence.
| Source test | Action / expected result | Relevant API / screen activity |
| TST-001 / AC-001 | Same-key case twice → one case/identical response | API-003; SCR-001/002 |
| TST-002 / AC-002 | Changed body/key →409 IDEMPOTENCY_CONFLICT | API-003 |
| TST-003 / T-01 / AC-003 | Valid foreign-tenant ID/token → non-disclosing404-equivalent; domain/RLS denial | Resource APIs |
| TST-004 / T-08 / AC-004 | Revoke indexed ACL → next query excludes; additionally revoke **during search** | API-012/021/022 |
| TST-005 / AC-005 | Forced schema invalid model → MODEL_OUTPUT_INVALID/no publish | API-037/run |
| TST-006 / T-03 / AC-006 | Prior/wrong hash approval after revision → stale rejection/audit | API-010 |
| TST-007 / T-07 / AC-007 | Replay outbox; same event **100 times** → exactly one accepted business transition | Event consumers |
| TST-008 / AC-008 | Provider429 burst → capped retries/controlled admission; saved cases remain available | Run/model admission |
| TST-009 / AC-009 | Missing citations → review OR unsupported, selection unresolved | Generation |
| TST-010 / AC-010 | Expire review → no approval/escalation recorded | Review |
| TST-011 / AC-011 | Keyboard-only case open → no blocked action/visible focus | SCR-002 consumer |
| TST-012 / AC-012 | Recovery exercise → stated RPO/RTO with safety | Recovery |
| TST-013 / AC-013 | Held tenant purge → protected records retained/receipted | API-017/041 |
| TST-014 / AC-014 | Arbitrary MCP → DENY before dispatch | API-046 |
| TST-015 / T-04 / AC-015 | Unsafe PDF/polyglot/zipped hostile input → scan/sandbox/bounded parse/quarantine/no index | API-006; zipped test is not supported format |
| TST-016 / AC-016 | Safety-regressed canary → blocked promotion | Release gates |

Additional required negative tests: hostile PDF instructions with evidence delimiting/pinned tools (`T-02`); credential observation in traces/provider requests (`T-05`); regional outage/approved fallback (`T-06`); historical audit edit/hash-chain protection (`T-09`); recursive tool hints/budgets (`T-10`); single Admin export denial/two-person manifest (`T-11`); replaced score fixtures/versioned signed dataset (`T-12`). [Source: p.88; `api:r1:c140:f2`, `api:r1:c140:f5`, `api:r1:c140:f6`, `api:r1:c140:f9`, `api:r1:c140:f10`, `api:r1:c140:f11`, `api:r1:c140:f12`]
Also verify:
- Authoritative revision/nonmutation guards, exactly one audit record per accepted transition, duplicate outcome without business reapplication and delayed-event safety.

- Current source ACL before generation/next retrieval and publication reauthorization after permission changes; source inspection/exact review display/required-field UI gating; refresh and scoped SSE replay.
- Unsafe-versus-low-quality distinction, durable accepted metadata after failed indexing, queued credential revoke, incomplete provisioning block and index-coverage readiness.
- No public datastores; private tenancy predicates/pool reset/workspace integrity; no secrets in public responses/model/tool undeclared scopes or document diagnostic telemetry.
- Full create→ingest→retrieve→draft→review→publish journey, rejected rework, poisoned quarantine, foreign search denial.
- Provider429 storms, lost worker heartbeats, duplicate events, object access failure and primary-region outage, measuring safety **and** recovery time.

Critical isolation/approval tests permit **zero exceptions**. `SEC-001`–`SEC-012` are release-blocking; a security-control owner independently reviews/reproduces negative evidence and signs release record. No mapping to `T-01`–`T-12` is supplied. Unmitigated critical isolation/approval bypass blocks promotion regardless of benchmarks. Low statistical confidence also blocks release; independent prompt/model roll-forward requires reevaluation. [Source: pp.74–76,88; `api:r1:c125:f2`, `api:r1:c128:f6`, `api:r1:c140:f13`, `api:r1:c140:f14`]

Fixtures are synthetic and cover successful/empty/mixed-permission/adversarial/malformed inputs; randomized tests record seeds; evaluation corpus is frozen/versioned/independently leakage-reviewed. Pipeline minimum: unit, schema evolution, negative authorization, workflow replay, staging connector sync, visual accessibility, search recall, grounding, policy recall, load and disaster recovery. Outputs are signed/release-digest linked; signature/report/statistical contracts remain open. [Source: p.89 E.1–E.2; `api:r1:c141:f17`, `api:r1:c141:f18`, `api:r1:c141:f19`, `api:r1:c141:f20`]

# 3. Data Specification
## Data Inventory and Relationships
### DAT-001 — Authority, scope and conventions

**Confirmed.** This is `03_data.md`, Stage 3 of 8, for OrionDesk AI, `OD-AI-DDS-001`, `R1.0`, design revision `1.3`. It integrates supplied chapter evidence, not a new inspection of unavailable attachments. The candidate remains provisional pending evidence review. **Confirmed** means supported for the fictional reference system; **Needs confirmation** means an incomplete contract or unresolved decision. No new **Proposal** is selected.

All citations below use **1794353355-OrionDesk_AI_Detailed_Design_Specification.pdf** and original pages. The source states: “All numbers are design assumptions, not measured production performance.” Figures are normative boundary illustrations, not generated implementation artifacts. Logical components, arrows, access scopes and register ownership categories do not independently establish tables, cardinalities or organizational data ownership. [pp.1–2; `data:r2:c1:f1`–`data:r2:c1:f4`, `data:r2:c2:f1`–`data:r2:c2:f3`]

Preserve identifiers in [01_screen_functions.md](01_screen_functions.md) and [02_api.md](02_api.md). `DAT-*` identifiers are specification traceability identifiers, not source namespace mappings. Browser routes and physical-to-wire aliases are not inferred.

The data scope includes enterprise knowledge/cases, grounded evidence, deterministic policy, review/publication, audit and operational evidence. Physical automation, irreversible financial transactions, fine-tuning, unrestricted browsing and agent cloud-administration permissions are **Out of scope**. Application-hosted GPU inference is excluded. Cross-region active/active mutation, OCR beyond English and customer-managed model weights are deferred. [pp.9–10,19; `data:r2:c7:f1`, `data:r2:c8:f6`, `data:r2:c25:f2`]
### DAT-002 — Storage authority and ownership
| Store/responsibility | Confirmed purpose and authority | Implementation qualification |
| PostgreSQL | Authoritative mutable metadata; case transactional state | Source-named reference product, not an independently selected new product |
| Private encrypted blob/object storage | Source and normalized artifacts, immutable versions | Provider, literal layout and crypto implementation unresolved |
| Vector/keyword search | Nonauthoritative searchable derivatives | Eventually consistent; cannot confer authorization |
| Cache | Versioned ephemeral results with short TTLs | CacheEntry ledger classification unresolved; no numerical result TTL supplied |
| Case Service | Transactional mutations | Concrete table ownership incomplete |
| Ingestion Service | Document conversion | Parser/catalog ownership details incomplete |
| Retrieval Service | Cited chunks | Search/evidence physical ownership incomplete |
| Orchestrator | Run state, bounded workflow | No direct DB credentials; narrowly scoped APIs |
| Policy Service | Binding approval requirements | Deterministic policy authority, not model decision |
| Engineering domain/platform/AI-platform teams | Case/policy APIs; identity/messaging; model-gateway contracts respectively | Contract ownership, not automatic entity stewardship |

Datastores have no public IP/endpoints. Workload identities are scoped and not shared between deployment units; managed identity replaces static credentials where supported. [pp.9,15–19; `data:r2:c8:f1`–`data:r2:c8:f2`, `data:r2:c18:f5`, `data:r2:c19:f1`, `data:r2:c19:f5`, `data:r2:c24:f1`, `data:r2:c24:f5`]

## Data Field Definitions
### DAT-005 — Reference `cases` physical declarations
All fields below are reference persistence declarations, not browser/API defaults. No additional index, type or product is independently selected. [p.86 B.2; `data:r2:c138:f20`–`data:r2:c138:f28`]
| Physical name | Meaning/type | Nullability/default | Key/value constraint |
| `id` | Case identifier; `UUID` | Primary key; no default shown | `PRIMARY KEY`; UUIDv7 generation separately scoped, not supplied SQL |
| `tenant_id` | Tenant; `UUID` | `NOT NULL`; no default shown | `REFERENCES tenants(id)` |
| `workspace_id` | Workspace; `UUID` | `NOT NULL`; no default shown | `REFERENCES workspaces(id)` |
| `status` | Case lifecycle; `TEXT` | `NOT NULL`; no default shown | CHECK six literals below |
| `revision` | Aggregate revision; `BIGINT` | `NOT NULL DEFAULT 1` | No positive-value CHECK/increment SQL shown |
| `sensitivity` | Classification; `TEXT` | `NOT NULL DEFAULT 'INTERNAL'` | No sensitivity CHECK or length shown |
| `created_at` | Creation time; `TIMESTAMPTZ` | `NOT NULL DEFAULT now()` | Precision/encoding unresolved |
| `updated_at` | Update time; `TIMESTAMPTZ` | `NOT NULL DEFAULT now()` | No automatic update trigger shown |

Additional constraint: `UNIQUE (tenant_id, id)`, alongside—not instead of—the `id` primary key. Status CHECK values are `NEW`, `TRIAGED`, `IN_PROGRESS`, `PENDING_APPROVAL`, `RESOLVED`, `CLOSED`. Lengths, final indexing strategy and omitted fields remain **Needs confirmation**.
Preserve reference tenancy SQL:
```sql
ALTER TABLE cases ENABLE ROW LEVEL SECURITY;
CREATE POLICY tenant_scope ON cases
USING (tenant_id = current_setting('app.tenant_id')::UUID);

**Confirmed production qualifications:** reset scoped connection-pool session variables **after every transaction**. Additionally enforce workspace-tenancy membership via foreign keys **or controlled write procedures**; the alternative is not selected. Independent `tenant_id` and `workspace_id` FKs alone do not establish membership. Role/bypass settings, context assignment/reset mechanics, missing-setting behavior and complete all-table policies are **Needs confirmation**.

raw_line_en: ## Lifecycle and Consistency
### DAT-009 — Tenant and referential integrity
1. Bind authenticated principal/tenant to requests; authorize role, workspace membership, sensitivity, source ACL, action and separation as applicable.
2. Re-evaluate resource attributes inside domain transactions and apply RLS. Every storage predicate includes tenant identity.
3. Reject cross-tenant substitutions with the absent-ID not-found response class, without revealing private existence; denial audit may retain principal and denied resource class.

4. Apply current ACL before retrieval text reaches generation and again at publication after permission changes. Ranking, immutable versions, cached results and prior approval never grant continuing access.

OIDC authorization-code flow uses PKCE and issuer/audience/expiry/subject/tenant token concepts. Reject unexpected algorithms/missing tenancy; no long-lived browser-local-storage refresh tokens. Optional secure `HttpOnly`, `SameSite` BFF cookies are unselected. [pp.21–23,34,51,89; `data:r2:c30:f1`, `data:r2:c30:f5`, `data:r2:c31:f1`, `data:r2:c31:f5`, `data:r2:c32:f1`, `data:r2:c32:f5`, `data:r2:c53:f2`, `data:r2:c83:f2`, `data:r2:c141:f3`]
### DAT-010 — Case and asynchronous-job lifecycle

**Case creation/read/update:** API-003 creates idempotently (`201`), starting `NEW`; classification is asynchronous. API-004 reads authorized current revision (`200`). API-005 PATCH uses `If-Match` (`200/409`). Actor/request-fingerprint outcomes are retained for24 hours; identical same-key creation yields one case/identical response, changed-body reuse yields `409 IDEMPOTENCY_CONFLICT`. Conflict returns `CASE_VERSION_CONFLICT` and current revision without changing business state. Long-running-job POST mutations transport `Idempotency-Key`; its complete scope/fingerprint/expiry contract remains open. [pp.12,25,54,83–84,89; `data:r2:c13:f1`, `data:r2:c37:f4`–`data:r2:c37:f5`, `data:r2:c90:f5`, `data:r2:c137:f6`–`data:r2:c137:f8`, `data:r2:c137:f21`, `data:r2:c141:f1`–`data:r2:c141:f2`]
| Case transition | Confirmed rule |
| `NEW → TRIAGED` | Role/revision/approval guards as applicable |
| `TRIAGED → IN_PROGRESS` | Supported |
| `IN_PROGRESS → PENDING_APPROVAL` or `RESOLVED` | Supported |
| `PENDING_APPROVAL → RESOLVED` or `IN_PROGRESS` | Supported |
| `CLOSED` | Final **unless explicitly reopened as a new revision** |

Closing edge/actor, reopening endpoint/target state and complete predicates remain **Needs confirmation**. Closure snapshots approved answer, cited versions and reviewer decisions as immutable approved-output lineage. [pp.25–26,82; `data:r2:c37:f1`, `data:r2:c38:f6`, `data:r2:c137:f2`]

**Mandatory job tenancy:** “Background jobs carry immutable tenant identity in signed envelopes.” Signing and tenant-identity immutability are separate confirmed obligations for classification, ingestion, synchronization, workflow, replay, provisioning/export/purge and other actual background jobs. Do **not** classify the entire job record immutable. Envelope schema, signature algorithm/keys and verification remain **Needs confirmation**. This also applies beside DAT-012 and DAT-017; canonical events/general tenant context do not substitute. [p.22 §5.3.1; `data:r2:c32:f2`]

raw_line_en: ### DAT-013 — Review, publication and histories

1. Select policy reviewer pool/minimum role/separation; own-high-risk self-approval is prohibited. Appendix B's unqualified “no self approval” leaves broader scope unresolved—no lower-risk permission is granted.
2. Show exact candidate, citations, model/prompt version and policy reasons. Source inspection is available before approval. Required review inputs gate UI actions; their names/types remain open.

3. API-010 (`200/409`) binds decision to reviewed hash. Changed/wrong-hash or unauthorized decisions reject stale/denied, preserve business state and audit denial. Decision records are immutable; annotations explicitly optional.

4. Review states: `ASSIGNED`, `OPENED`, `APPROVED`, `REJECTED`, `EXPIRED`, guarded by actor/hash/separation. Configured expiry reassigns/escalates without approval; TST-010 records escalation. Branch/SLA remain open.
5. Overrides require elevated role, secondary reviewer and audited reason. Denied rework creates new run revisions, never retroactive approval.

6. Publication is distinct: validate exact artifact/evidence/versioned policy and current permissions. Unapproved high-risk cannot publish. Commit final pointer and satisfied gate atomically; old approvals cannot publish changed artifacts. `ApprovalDecisionRecorded` consumer **validates publication**, not automatically publishes.

`case_revisions` and `audit_events` are append-only. Approved source versions/decision lineage are immutable; assignment/form immutable-subject conflicts remain DAT-020, not permission to rewrite history.
### DAT-014 — Transactions, concurrency and replay
1. Validate before transaction, at domain invariants and before tool dispatch; client validation is convenience only.
2. Reject stale/unauthorized business writes before relevant publication; preserve business state. Denial/duplicate evidence is not an accepted business transition.

3. Apply stated case-mutation/approval/outbox ACID boundary as applicable. Do not infer every case mutation also approves another record. Search/webhook changes are asynchronous and reconciled; state-changing workflows use outbox or explicitly reconciled saga.
4. At-least-once consumers check event/operation identity, ledger and aggregate revision. Record duplicates and do not reapply. Detect delayed/stale revisions without cross-partition order reliance.
5. Each accepted transition has one audit record and tenant-scoped traces; correlated event logs/audit exclude document text in diagnostics.
6. Transient retries are bounded exponential backoff/jitter/per-dependency breakers. Validation/permission failures are permanent and never retry.
7. Operator replay requires reason, dry run and bounded scope. Preserve original event identity **except** schema-transforming migration with explicit provenance linkage.

8. Expand-contract migrations add nullable columns, backfill bounded batches then enforce constraints; active readers must not lose fields. Initial migration nullability is not final business nullability.

DAT-016 — Audit, retention and controlled exit
raw_line_en: ### DAT-016 — Audit, retention and controlled exit

section_en: DAT-016 — Audit, retention and controlled exit
DAT-016 — Audit, retention and controlled exit
raw_line_en: Audit is append-only, batch-hash chained and exported to independently controlled retention storage. Operators query but never alter historical review decisions; Auditor scope is redacted/nonediting. Diagnostic logs have30-day **default** TTL; security audit follows a distinct7-year **fictional** policy. Corporate retention selection remains unresolved. Purges record receipts/legal-hold exceptions; do not apply diagnostic TTL to security audit. Retention jobs consider only eligible closed cases; CLOSED alone is not eligibility. [pp.11–12,26,62,66; `data:r2:c12:f6`, `data:r2:c38:f7`, `data:r2:c104:f1`, `data:r2:c110:f5`]

section_en: DAT-016 — Audit, retention and controlled exit
DAT-016 — Audit, retention and controlled exit
raw_line_en: Export/delete both require two independent approval checks and `Admin + approver` scope. Export explicitly requires **two-person approval plus manifest**; single Admin fails. Export contains case metadata, approved artifacts, source references and checksum audit manifests, excluding secrets/internal prompts. Deletion honors holds, writes tombstones, removes blobs/index entries and records receipts; held protected records are retained/receipted. Soft-deleted entities cannot be retrieved; final purge is scheduled tombstone processing. API-016/017 `202` is acceptance, not completion. Data-subject access uses the same inventory, not an invented endpoint. Tenant/workspace scope, partial receipts and lineage purge remain open. DAT-015 vault/rotation rules remain binding during retention/exit. [pp.51,78–80,83,88–89; `data:r2:c84:f6`, `data:r2:c131:f1`, `data:r2:c134:f1`, `data:r2:c134:f5`, `data:r2:c137:f19`–`data:r2:c137:f20`, `data:r2:c140:f11`, `data:r2:c141:f13`]

raw_line_en: ### BAT-001–003 — Classification, synchronization and backfill

1. **BAT-001:** consume CaseCreated case ID/revision in tenant scope; process NEW intake/business context and attach policy-aware labels, confidences and provenance. User correction requires reason code. Label domains, algorithm, attachment-completeness predicate, authorized correction interface and classification completion state remain BAT-OQ-006. Do not merge this event with RunRequested or assume run launch emits CaseCreated. [pp.12,87; `batch_functions:r1:c13:f1`, `batch_functions:r1:c139:f1`]

2. **BAT-002:** require complete provisioning and configured provider; inspect advertised list/fetch/delta cursor/ACL/delete support. Unsupported capabilities produce an explicit visible lower-trust warning, never silent assumptions or ACL bypass. Resolve workspace vault references; revoked queued credentials fail `CONNECTOR_REAUTH_REQUIRED` without token disclosure. Already-running revocation behavior remains open. [pp.27–28,78; `batch_functions:r1:c42:f1`, `batch_functions:r1:c42:f5`, `batch_functions:r1:c132:f2`]

3. Persist provider cursor/high-watermark/error ledger. Advance only after durable preceding ingestion outcomes. Partial batches retry safely. After bounded retries quarantine malformed items with reason/correlation/remediation; **remaining batch may proceed while ledger records the exception**. Continuation is permitted, not mandatory; quarantined item is not declared successful. Exact outcome/advancement predicate remains open. [pp.28–29; `batch_functions:r1:c43:f1`, `batch_functions:r1:c44:f6`]

4. Honor `Retry-After`, exponential backoff/jitter, workspace quotas and fair scheduling so a large tenant cannot starve smaller workspaces. No quota/batch/retry number is selected. [p.28; `batch_functions:r1:c44:f1`]

5. Source deletion creates tombstone/scheduled index removal. ACL changes invalidate affected cache before serving new results; revoked access applies before next retrieval even during cleanup. [pp.27–29; `batch_functions:r1:c41:f2`, `batch_functions:r1:c43:f4`, `batch_functions:r1:c43:f5`]

6. **BAT-003:** ingest historic sources in bounded windows using stable source IDs and per-batch reconciliation receipts. Determine search readiness from indexed coverage, **not merely queue emptiness**. Receipt schema, window bounds, coverage threshold, no-input and whole-run completion remain BAT-OQ-006. [p.78; `batch_functions:r1:c132:f7`, `batch_functions:r1:c132:f8`]

Targets include `connector_cursors(connector_id,cursor,watermark,retry_state)` and source/version catalogs. `watermark` is not an approved wire alias for high-watermark. [p.85; `batch_functions:r1:c138:f3`, `batch_functions:r1:c138:f7`; DAT-003/016]

section_en: BAT-004–006 — Ingestion, index promotion and reconciliation
raw_line_en: ### BAT-004–006 — Ingestion, index promotion and reconciliation

section_en: BAT-004–006 — Ingestion, index promotion and reconciliation
BAT-004–006 — Ingestion, index promotion and reconciliation
raw_line_en: 1. Admit only R1PDF/DOCX/HTML/UTF-8 text with MIME signature/extension agreement, configurable **25MB per file**, and decompression-bomb protection. MIME literals, MB convention and bomb/sandbox thresholds remain open. ZIP appears only as a hostile test fixture, not an admitted format.

section_en: BAT-004–006 — Ingestion, index promotion and reconciliation
raw_line_en: 2. Scan before parse. Disable macros; do not fetch embedded remote references. Unsafe attachments quarantine and never enter search.

section_en: BAT-004–006 — Ingestion, index promotion and reconciliation
raw_line_en: 3. Preserve PDF block page index/bbox, table rows/columns, heading/reading order for chunking. OCR is opt-in and provenance-marked; beyond-English OCR deferred.

section_en: BAT-004–006 — Ingestion, index promotion and reconciliation
raw_line_en: 4. Normalize transport artifacts without rewriting source claims. Content fingerprint plus pipeline version identifies immutable derivatives; revised processing may coexist side by side rather than overwrite history.

section_en: BAT-004–006 — Ingestion, index promotion and reconciliation
raw_line_en: 5. Store chunk URI/file hash/page/**optional** bbox. PDF block mandatory bbox does not make chunk bbox mandatory. Quality indicators include empty-page ratio, unknown-character ratio, table loss and language confidence. Low-quality authorized documents remain viewable but excluded from autonomous recommendations; low quality is not automatically unsafe quarantine. Thresholds/indexability/status mapping remain BAT-OQ-007.

section_en: BAT-004–006 — Ingestion, index promotion and reconciliation
raw_line_en: 6. `DocumentNormalized`, Ingestion version ID/source hash, builds index. Search rows contain tenant/workspace/document-version/chunk/language/classification, normalized keyword text and **1536-dimensional** embedding.

section_en: BAT-004–006 — Ingestion, index promotion and reconciliation
raw_line_en: 7. Rebuild a parallel index; switch versioned read alias atomically only after completeness and recall checks. Database remains authoritative. `SearchIndexCommitted`, Indexer generation/document revision, invalidates query cache. Promotion arbitration, thresholds and retired-generation policy remain open.

section_en: BAT-004–006 — Ingestion, index promotion and reconciliation
raw_line_en: 8. Failed index write **does not roll back accepted source metadata**. BAT-006 compares fingerprints/retries and repairs broken links from outbox. Apply permanent-error nonretry; no unrestricted repair loop is authorized. Reconciliation successful completion/receipt and selection remain open.

raw_line_en: ### BAT-007–009 — Grounded workflow, review expiry and publication

section_en: BAT-007–009 — Grounded workflow, review expiry and publication
BAT-007–009 — Grounded workflow, review expiry and publication
raw_line_en: 1. Create accepted run immediately; persist DAG plan revision before side effects. Depth **8**, maximum **16** tool invocations, explicit dependencies/replayable checkpoints. Persist each stage checkpoint before downstream dispatch.

section_en: BAT-007–009 — Grounded workflow, review expiry and publication
raw_line_en: 2. Retrieve only current permitted evidence before releasing text to generation. Form lexical/normalized vector queries, bounded candidates, reciprocal rank fusion, deterministic rerank, document/source diversity and per-query token budget. Ranking never authorizes. Evidence includes chunk ID/source title/document revision/page anchor/ACL digest; citation identifiers are opaque/verified.

section_en: BAT-007–009 — Grounded workflow, review expiry and publication
raw_line_en: 3. If confidence **OR** quality insufficient, return `NO_SUPPORTED_EVIDENCE`, never fabricated context. Clarification **OR** human routing remains unselected; missing citations produce needs-review **OR** unsupported under TST-009, not a chosen universal state.

section_en: BAT-007–009 — Grounded workflow, review expiry and publication
raw_line_en: 4. Whitelist approved deployments by capability/region/handling/context/cost/evaluation. Reserve input/output tokens and track provider usage under workspace quota. Exhaustion is terminal for current run without automatic model/data-class change. Approved fallback requires equal-or-stronger handling and approved region/deployment; no restricted content in unapproved region on outage.

section_en: BAT-007–009 — Grounded workflow, review expiry and publication
raw_line_en: 5. Compose fixed rules, signed workflow instruction, validated user input and delimited untrusted passages; strip evidence tool directives and record injection indicators. Model text never authorizes. Versioned JSON parsing has bounded retries; unknown fields, invalid citations/control injection produce `MODEL_OUTPUT_INVALID` and no publication.

section_en: BAT-007–009 — Grounded workflow, review expiry and publication
raw_line_en: 6. Dispatch only pinned approved MCP schemas/validated arguments/scoped service credentials. External writes need separate capability, mutable calls idempotency and consequential human authorization. Discovery/A2A registration grants no permission; receivers may decline; denied actions cannot be replaced by equivalent tools.

section_en: BAT-007–009 — Grounded workflow, review expiry and publication
raw_line_en: 7. Normalize/store policy sensitivity/action/evidence quality/model class/financial impact/confidence with rule version. Deterministic outcomes: `AUTO_ALLOW`, `HUMAN_REVIEW`, `REQUEST_MORE_EVIDENCE`, `DENY`; model tags cannot override. High-impact becomes review task, not autonomous mutation.

section_en: BAT-007–009 — Grounded workflow, review expiry and publication
raw_line_en: 8. Select policy reviewer pool/minimum role/separation. Display exact candidate/citations/model-prompt version/policy reasons and inspectable anchored source. Required review fields gate Approve/Reject UI, not authorization. Record decision/actor/time/hash/rationale and optional annotations; changed/wrong-hash decisions stale-reject/audit with unchanged business state.

section_en: BAT-007–009 — Grounded workflow, review expiry and publication
raw_line_en: 9. On configured-SLA expiry reassign **OR** escalate without approval. TST-010 requires escalation recorded. SLA/time basis/branch/recipients and no-expired-task result remain open. Overrides require elevated role/secondary reviewer/audited reason; denied rework is new run revision, never retroactive approval.

section_en: BAT-007–009 — Grounded workflow, review expiry and publication
raw_line_en: 10. ApprovalDecisionRecorded **validates** publication. Recompute current authorization after permission changes and reject stale evidence. Required evidence/satisfied versioned policy/exact hash apply; unapproved high-risk cannot publish. Commit final response pointer and satisfied gate in the **same transaction**; replay cannot publish changed content under old approval.

raw_line_en: ### BAT-023 — Logging, notification and monitoring

Accepted transitions require **one audit record per accepted transition**, stable denial codes and tenant-scoped traces. Rejected stale/unauthorized business writes remain unchanged before relevant event publication. Duplicate/denial ledger evidence is not another accepted business transition and must not be suppressed by that audit-count rule. Registered events remain visible through correlated logs/audit with no source document text in diagnostics. [pp.48–50; `batch_functions:r1:c79:f10`, `batch_functions:r1:c82:f1`, `batch_functions:r1:c82:f3`, `batch_functions:r1:c80:f9`]

Every request carries `trace_id`/`correlation_id`; child DB/connector/retrieval/model/approval spans contain identifiers/policy outcomes, **not documents/API secrets**. Logs default counts/digests; policy-conditional PII minimization does not waive hard secrecy. Public errors exclude connector credentials/full prompts/retrieved documents/unauthorized existence. Preserve uppercase `CASE_VERSION_CONFLICT`, `IDEMPOTENCY_CONFLICT`, `MODEL_OUTPUT_INVALID`, `CONNECTOR_REAUTH_REQUIRED`, `NO_SUPPORTED_EVIDENCE`; convention/schema/recovery remain open. Monitor request/error rate/latency/saturation, grounding pass/empty retrieval/provider throttling/token usage/approval backlog, queue oldest age/index backlog/outbox lag/parser flags/ACL revision. Worker scaling uses queue age/throughput; numeric thresholds open. Pages are for user-impacting incidents; routine spend anomalies create owner/threshold tickets. Provider-outage page only if availability budget affected; disable generation admission/preserve manual/evidence/display degraded.429+Retry-After controls new runs while saved cases remain. Optional lexical degradation needs visible reduced-quality flag. No degraded recovery bypasses safety. # 5. Business Rules
## Rule Inventory and Scope
### BR-001 — Authority and interpretation

**Confirmed.** This Stage 5 specification, `05_business_rules.md`, applies to OrionDesk AI, `OD-AI-DDS-001`, `R1.0 / revision 1.3`, a controlled fictional reference architecture. It consolidates supplied chapter judgments, not a new inspection of attachments. The candidate remains provisional pending evidence review.

**Confirmed** identifies reference-system obligations; **Needs confirmation** identifies missing implementation contracts or unresolved source conflicts. No new **Proposal** is selected. All numbers retain the source qualification: “All numbers are design assumptions, not measured production performance.” Figures are normative boundary illustrations, not generated implementation artifacts. Fictional identities, UI metrics, grants and configuration values are not production defaults or approvals. Contents are navigation, not independent evidence of behavior. ## Decisions, Calculations, and State Transitions
### BR-002–003 — Authority and access

**Confirmed.** “Untrusted retrieved documents and LLM responses cannot authorize tools, change tenant scope, alter approvals or bypass the versioned deterministic policy engine.” Browser-supplied arbitrary tool definitions are prohibited. Source/model content remains data, including hostile instructions, recursive hints and displayed capability grants. Discovery, registration, schema validity and relevance confer no permission. [PDF p.7; `business_rules:r1:c4:f2`, `business_rules:r1:c4:f5`; pp.40–42,87; `business_rules:r1:c65:f2`, `business_rules:r1:c68:f7`, `business_rules:r1:c139:f11`]
| Condition | Required decision / result | Qualification |
| Authenticated request | Bind principal and tenant; evaluate role, tenant, workspace membership, case sensitivity, source ACL, action and separation | Role/screen visibility alone insufficient |
| Interactive session | Authorization-code flow with PKCE; token issuer/audience/expiry/subject/tenant concepts | Reject unexpected algorithms and missing tenancy; exact values/lifetimes open |
| Browser refresh credential | No long-lived refresh token in local storage | Secure `HttpOnly`, `SameSite` BFF cookie is optional, not selected |

| Domain access | Re-evaluate attributes within transaction; tenant context/RLS; every storage predicate contains tenant | Pool context reset after **every transaction**; additional workspace membership FK **OR** controlled-write enforcement mandatory, choice open |
| Background job | Signed envelope with immutable tenant identity | Whole job and permissions are not frozen |
| Foreign resource substitution | Absent-ID not-found response class, no private-existence disclosure | Foreign case test requires `404-equivalent non-disclosing`; universal body/status unspecified |
| Retrieved chunk | Originating ACL filter before text reaches model | Ranking and immutable version do not authorize |
| Permission change after search | Recompute publication authorization; reject stale evidence | Earlier search/review not continuing authority |

[PDF pp.21–23 §§5.1–5.3; `business_rules:r1:c30:f1`, `business_rules:r1:c30:f5`, `business_rules:r1:c31:f1`, `business_rules:r1:c31:f2`, `business_rules:r1:c32:f1`, `business_rules:r1:c32:f2`, `business_rules:r1:c32:f7`; pp.51,86,89; `business_rules:r1:c83:f2`, `business_rules:r1:c138:f14`, `business_rules:r1:c138:f15`, `business_rules:r1:c141:f3`]

**Out of scope:** physical automation, irreversible financial transactions, foundation-model fine-tuning, unrestricted browsing, agent administrative-cloud permissions and application-hosted GPU inference. Financial-impact evaluation and usage accounting are not themselves excluded. **Deferred:** active/active cross-region mutation, OCR beyond English and customer-managed weights. [PDF pp.9–10,19; `business_rules:r1:c7:f1`, `business_rules:r1:c8:f7`, `business_rules:r1:c25:f2`]
### BR-004–005 — Case rules and calculations
1. An authorized Analyst creates an idempotent case, reference `201`, beginning `NEW`.
2. Asynchronous classification attaches labels, confidences and provenance. Label correction requires a reason code; actor/catalog/intake completeness are **Needs confirmation**.
3. Case mutation submits `If-Match`. Conflicting revision returns `409 CASE_VERSION_CONFLICT` with current revision and unchanged business state.

4. Actor/request-fingerprint idempotency maps one outcome for **24 hours**. Same-key duplicate creation produces one case and identical response; changed-body reuse returns `409 IDEMPOTENCY_CONFLICT`. Window origin/expiry equality/fingerprint/concurrent admission remain open.
5. Apply role/revision/approval guards to supported transitions. Do not add missing closing/reopening edges.
| Source state | Supported destination | Condition / exception |
| NEW | TRIAGED | Applicable guards |
| TRIAGED | IN_PROGRESS | Applicable guards |
| IN_PROGRESS | PENDING_APPROVAL or RESOLVED | Branch guards undefined |
| PENDING_APPROVAL | RESOLVED or IN_PROGRESS | Branch guards undefined |
| CLOSED | Final, **unless explicitly reopened as a new revision** | Reopen actor/action/destination and transition into CLOSED undefined |

[PDF pp.12,24–26,82–84,89; `business_rules:r1:c13:f1`, `business_rules:r1:c36:f4`, `business_rules:r1:c37:f1`, `business_rules:r1:c37:f4`, `business_rules:r1:c37:f5`, `business_rules:r1:c137:f6`, `business_rules:r1:c137:f8`, `business_rules:r1:c141:f1`, `business_rules:r1:c141:f2`]
| Calculation / setting | Confirmed constraint | Needs confirmation beside implementation |
| Priority | Derive from explicit impact and urgency, never model output alone | Domains, formula, ties, units, rounding, precedence and whether model may contribute alongside inputs |
| Contractual deadline | Business calendar computes in workspace timezone | Start, duration, working hours, holidays, DST, rounding and calendar version |
| Breach prediction | Advisory; cannot alter contractual deadline | Prediction method/confidence/threshold |
| Workspace settings | Retention class, allowed models, credential references, approved tools and reviewer routing | Values and administrative permission/endpoint |
| Configuration change | Revision precondition plus durable audit | Conflict/activation/version selection |
| Configurable numeric threshold | Explicitly versioned policy | Effective periods, selection and reevaluation |
[PDF pp.24–25 §§6.1/6.3, p.9 §1.2.2; `business_rules:r1:c36:f1`, `business_rules:r1:c38:f1`, `business_rules:r1:c38:f2`, `business_rules:r1:c7:f6`]

Reference `cases` DDL has UUID keys, six status CHECK literals, `revision BIGINT NOT NULL DEFAULT 1`, `sensitivity TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT 'INTERNAL'` and creation/update `TIMESTAMPTZ DEFAULT now()`. These are persistence declarations, not UI defaults, publication permissions or automatic update triggers. Append-only `case_revisions` is distinct from mutable case state. [PDF pp.85–86; `business_rules:r1:c138:f3`, `business_rules:r1:c138:f9`, `business_rules:r1:c138:f10`, `business_rules:r1:c138:f11`, `business_rules:r1:c138:f12`]
### BR-006–008 — Documents, synchronization and retrieval
| Prerequisite / condition | Required result | Open boundary |
| File admission | R1 PDF, DOCX, HTML, UTF-8 text; MIME signature/extension agreement; configurable **25 MB/file**; bomb protection | MIME literals, MB convention, cap equality and bomb threshold |
| Before parsing | Scan, disable macros, no embedded remote fetch | Scanner failure/remediation contract |
| Unsafe attachment | Quarantine, no indexing | ZIP/polyglot are hostile tests, not admitted formats |
| PDF extraction | Page/block bboxes, table row/column metadata, heading/reading order | Coordinate units/page basis/chunking method |
| OCR fallback | Opt-in and provenance-marked | Actor/control/trigger/marker; beyond-English deferred |
| Normalization | Remove transport artifacts, never rewrite claims; fingerprint + pipeline version immutable derivatives may coexist | Hash/serialization/reprocess/retention mechanics |
| Every chunk | Source URI/hash/page, optional bbox | Block bbox does not make chunk bbox mandatory |
| Generation citation | Resolvable stored anchor **AND** current access permission | Missing-anchor/error/recovery |
| Low extraction quality | Authorized document viewable, excluded autonomous recommendation | Empty-page/unknown-character/table-loss/language-confidence formulas/thresholds and index/state mapping |
| Missing connector capability | Explicit visible lower-trust warning | Safe restrictions for unsupported ACL/delete/delta; no ACL bypass |
| Revoked credential | Queued jobs fail `CONNECTOR_REAUTH_REQUIRED`, no token exposure | Already-running jobs/reauth timing |
| Sync progress | Cursor/high-watermark/error ledger; advance only after durable preceding outcomes | Atomicity, durable outcome catalog |

| Malformed item after bounded retries | Quarantine with reason/correlation/remediation; remaining batch **may** continue with ledger exception | Continue/stop choice and permanent-fault taxonomy; not poisoned-item success |
| Source deletion | Tombstone/scheduled index removal | Cleanup cadence open |
| Source ACL change | Invalidate cache before new results; revocation effective before next retrieval | During-search cancellation/release algorithm open; stale visibility is incident |
| Index rebuild | Parallel build, completeness/recall checks, atomic alias switch; database authoritative | Measures/thresholds/promotion arbitration |
| Failed index write | Keep accepted metadata; fingerprint reconciliation and outbox link repair | No unrestricted retry of permanent errors |

[PDF pp.27–36,49,88–89; `business_rules:r1:c42:f1`, `business_rules:r1:c42:f5`, `business_rules:r1:c43:f1`, `business_rules:r1:c43:f4`, `business_rules:r1:c43:f5`, `business_rules:r1:c44:f6`, `business_rules:r1:c44:f7`, `business_rules:r1:c48:f1`, `business_rules:r1:c48:f4`, `business_rules:r1:c48:f5`, `business_rules:r1:c49:f1`, `business_rules:r1:c49:f2`, `business_rules:r1:c49:f6`, `business_rules:r1:c50:f1`, `business_rules:r1:c50:f2`, `business_rules:r1:c50:f6`, `business_rules:r1:c50:f7`, `business_rules:r1:c54:f5`, `business_rules:r1:c79:f6`, `business_rules:r1:c140:f4`, `business_rules:r1:c141:f15`]

Retrieval uses scoped tenant/workspace/version/chunk/language/classification rows, normalized text and **1536-dimensional embeddings**. Form lexical and normalized vector queries; bounded candidate retrieval → reciprocal rank fusion → deterministic reranking → redundancy/source-diversity control, subject to model-token cap and ACL filtering. No RRF equation, constant, scoring tie rule or selected numeric candidate/token limit is supplied by this operative prose. Cache identity includes tenant, user-scope digest, ACL revision, query hash and index generation; authorization change purges before normal TTL and must satisfy the stronger next-retrieval rule. [PDF pp.34–36,53; `business_rules:r1:c54:f1`, `business_rules:r1:c55:f1`, `business_rules:r1:c55:f6`, `business_rules:r1:c86:f7`, `business_rules:r1:c86:f8`]

Every evidence item includes chunk ID, source title, document revision, page anchor and ACL digest; opaque citation identifiers are verified before display. Insufficient confidence **OR** quality returns `NO_SUPPORTED_EVIDENCE`, never fabricated context. Clarification **OR** human routing is permitted but unselected. Missing citations separately require needs-review **OR** unsupported outcome; do not silently choose a durable state. [PDF pp.35–36,89; `business_rules:r1:c56:f1`, `business_rules:r1:c56:f2`, `business_rules:r1:c56:f5`, `business_rules:r1:c56:f6`, `business_rules:r1:c141:f9`]

raw_line_en: ### BR-018 — Admission, containment and recovery

Admit new AI runs only when workspace tokens **AND** queue age **AND** provider capacity satisfy thresholds. Throttling uses `429` plus `Retry-After`, preserving saved cases. Generation outage disables new generation admission but preserves manual case editing/evidence search and shows degraded status. Optional lexical fallback during vector degradation requires a visible reduced-quality flag. Never bypass authorization/approval. Pages require user-impact incidents; routine spend creates owner/threshold tickets; provider-outage page only when availability budget impacted. [PDF pp.65,68–69,79; `business_rules:r1:c109:f7`, `business_rules:r1:c113:f2`, `business_rules:r1:c115:f1`, `business_rules:r1:c115:f4`, `business_rules:r1:c115:f5`, `business_rules:r1:c133:f1`]
| Reference value | Scope / boundary |
| 2000 daily users;60steady/180burst rps | Workload, not selected quotas |
| 100000 indexed documents/tenant maximum;20concurrent runs/large tenant | Reference envelope; large-tenant/admission definitions open |
| Typical1MB≈40–120chunks | Content/parser dependent approximation |
| API99.9% monthly | Objective, not observed result |
| Case P95 within300ms / under300ms | Equality and common measurement unresolved |
| Search P95<1.5s | Excludes remote fetch; model separately measured; equality fails strict clause |
| RPO≤15min;RTO≤4h | Reference recovery objectives, equality included; not backup intervals |

API scaling uses utilization/latency; extraction/embedding scaling queue age/throughput. Primary writes and warm recovery snapshot restore require incident command; continuous PostgreSQL backups and object/index-recipe joint tests apply. Chaos includes429 storms, lost heartbeats, duplicates, object failure and primary outage, measuring safety **and** recovery time. [PDF pp.19,65,68–70; `business_rules:r1:c25:f1`, `business_rules:r1:c25:f6`, `business_rules:r1:c109:f1`, `business_rules:r1:c109:f2`, `business_rules:r1:c114:f1`, `business_rules:r1:c114:f5`, `business_rules:r1:c116:f1`, `business_rules:r1:c116:f2`, `business_rules:r1:c116:f7`]

Provisioning idempotently creates policy/encryption refs/role bindings/quotas/connector stubs. Visible incomplete state blocks sync; historic readiness uses index coverage, not queue emptiness. [PDF p.78; `business_rules:r1:c132:f1`, `business_rules:r1:c132:f2`, `business_rules:r1:c132:f7`, `business_rules:r1:c132:f8`]
**Delayed-index procedure:**
1. Detect oldest queue age/backlog and identify tenant/generation.
2. Pause only faulty connector/indexer shard; preserve accepted source records.
3. Diagnose event/outbox/parser/throttling/ACL revision.
4. Replay validated outbox through bounded operator-controlled work.
5. Compare source fingerprints/index versions and run denied probes before closure; closure pass criteria open.
6. Link audit IDs/time window/blast radius/quality effect/preventative action.

Suspected ACL leakage separately suspends affected aliases/revokes evidence cache/preserves audit/scoped ACL replay; search restoration requires negative access tests **pass**. [PDF pp.79,90; `business_rules:r1:c133:f5`, `business_rules:r1:c142:f7`, `business_rules:r1:c142:f8`, `business_rules:r1:c142:f9`, `business_rules:r1:c142:f10`, `business_rules:r1:c142:f11`, `business_rules:r1:c142:f12`, `business_rules:r1:c142:f13`]

raw_line_en: 5. Security/SRE verify egress/secrets/backups/alerts before promotion. Bind/reconstruct image/schema/prompt/model-routing-policy versions.

raw_line_en: ### ERR-020 — Unavailable integration contract

Every source-named interface retains validation before long-running allocation. When a dependency is unavailable: **documented retryable error OR persisted asynchronous job identifier, never ambiguous success**. Neither alternative is universally selected. This applies across governance, case/run/attachment, identity/membership, health, connector/search/model, review, internal workflow/replay/storage, OpenAPI/SSE/evidence, audit/holds/usage/metrics/capacity, release/evaluation and exit interfaces.

Preserve the paths and inventory in API-003–042e; generic clauses do not invent new endpoints. In particular ordinary `200` reads/search/SSE, `201` creation and `202` ingestion/run/sync/evaluation/export/delete acceptance remain distinct. `202` is not READY, PUBLISHED, downloadable export or completed purge. No generic GET wording authorizes job allocation. **Needs confirmation:** dependency taxonomy, selection, allocation owner, durable ID/status/readback/lifetime, retryability and client presentation for each interface. raw_line_en: 1. Export/delete require **two independent approval checks** and `Admin + approver`. Export specifically needs **two-person approval plus manifest**; a single Admin fails. Do not silently extend person semantics to every deletion check.

section_en: ERR-024–027 — Exit, integrity, release and resilience
raw_line_en: 2. Export contains case metadata, approved artifacts, source references and checksum audit manifests; excludes secrets/internal prompts. Deletion enforces legal holds, tombstones, permitted blob/index removal and receipts. Held protected records remain **retained and receipted**; `202` is not completion. Tenant/workspace scope and partial completion remain open.

section_en: ERR-024–027 — Exit, integrity, release and resilience
raw_line_en: 3. Closure snapshots approved answer/cited versions/review decisions and preserves immutable lineage. Case retention only for eligible closed cases; CLOSED alone insufficient and explicit reopen-as-new-revision remains possible. Purge/reopen races and legally permitted lineage purge require decision.

section_en: ERR-024–027 — Exit, integrity, release and resilience
raw_line_en: 4. Audit/history/decisions remain append-only or immutable as declared. Operators may query, never edit historical review decisions. Vault/credential/encryption rotation obligations remain during recovery; exact rotation-failure response is open.

section_en: ERR-024–027 — Exit, integrity, release and resilience
raw_line_en: 5. Every storage predicate includes tenant; pool scoped variables reset after **every transaction including failed ones**. Production additionally enforces workspace-tenancy membership by FK **OR** controlled writes. Missing context/reset failure and SQL-to-business errors remain open.

section_en: ERR-024–027 — Exit, integrity, release and resilience
raw_line_en: 6. Compatible migration/canary/drain and signed build/config/evidence prerequisites apply. Unverified allowed-build digest cannot deploy. Regression triggers **automated traffic rollback, not DB down-migration**; general binary-first compensation only explicitly supported. Plans disclose whether new writes remain readable, not guarantee readability.

section_en: ERR-024–027 — Exit, integrity, release and resilience
raw_line_en: 7. Low statistical confidence blocks release; independent prompt/model changes require reevaluation. Critical isolation/approval tests have zero exceptions; unmitigated critical cross-tenant OR approval bypass blocks regardless benchmark. SEC-001–012 evidence independently reviewed/reproduced and release-signed.

section_en: ERR-024–027 — Exit, integrity, release and resilience
raw_line_en: 8. Primary writes/one warm region; snapshot restoration only under incident command. Reference **RPO≤15 min, RTO≤4 h**, continuous PostgreSQL backups and joint object/index-recipe checks. Lost heartbeats/object failures/primary outage need executable recovery contracts; objectives are not schedules.

raw_line_en: ## Logging, Monitoring, and Operations
### ERR-029 — Evidence and sensitivity contracts
| Evidence | Confirmed fields/conditions | Qualification |

| Request/span context | `trace_id`, `correlation_id`; child DB/connector/retrieval/model/approval spans; identifiers and policy outcomes | Provider trace independent; no alias/type/transport supplied |
| General boundary | tenant_id and actor context everywhere | Not editable UI fields |
| Durable-changing record | tenant_id, revision, actor_id, occurred_at, correlation ID | Only “wherever the operation changes durable state”; not universal GET write |

| Canonical event | event_id, type, schema_version, tenant_id, aggregate_id, aggregate_revision, occurred_at, trace_id, payload; UTC/canonical JSON | Canonicalization/types/aliases/version rules open; not SSE/job-envelope equivalence |
| Actual background job | Signed envelope, immutable tenant identity | Whole job/permissions not immutable; signature verification schema open |
| Accepted transition | One audit record, tenant-scoped trace | Separate denial/duplicate evidence retained |
| Denial | Stable non-sensitive code; foreign-resource audit principal and denied resource class | Most code literals and levels open |
| Duplicate | Event ledger/revision and recorded duplicate outcome | No mutation reapplication; schema/atomicity/retention open |
| Incident | Audit IDs, time window, blast radius, quality effect, preventative action | Link evidence, not invented receipt fields |

**Sensitive values:** public responses/errors never expose secrets/raw provider credentials, connector tokens, full prompts, retrieved documents or unauthorized existence. Safe structured validation details only. Diagnostic traces contain no user documents/API secrets; source text is absent from diagnostic telemetry. Policy-permitted nonessential PII redaction and default token/digest logs do not waive these prohibitions. Audit is independently retained, append-only/batch-hash chained; register SHA-256 source/revision does not select the chain algorithm. Diagnostic logs use **30-day default TTL**; security audit a separate **seven-year fictional policy**, with holds/receipts and corporate selection unresolved.
